title: InventoryMovement reporting: a fourth rowstore index is requested
prompt: Azure SQL Database 'RetailOps', General Purpose, 8 vCores, about 41.5 GB of memory, compatibility level 160, no readable secondary. Snapshot taken Thursday 2026-09-24 09:00 UTC. A platform failover reset the index usage counters on 2026-09-15 02:41, so they cover 9.26 days. Query Store holds data from 2026-09-11 only, because size-based cleanup has run. Month-end change freeze: 2026-09-30 18:00 to 2026-10-02 18:00. Flash sale on 2026-10-09 with a change freeze from 2026-10-08. Log rate cap: 36 MB/s. Space headroom: 213 GB.
The missing-index DMV reports for Q15: equality MovementType; inequality MovementAt; include ProductId, WarehouseId,
Qty, UnitCost; impact 91.2%. The advisor script wants CREATE INDEX IX_MI_InventoryMovement_1 ON
dbo.InventoryMovement (MovementType, MovementAt) INCLUDE (ProductId, WarehouseId, Qty, UnitCost). Decide what to
create, and which existing index must stay.

workload.description: Dashboard: inventory valuation over a 90-day window
sql: SELECT im.WarehouseId, im.MovementType, SUM(im.Qty), SUM(im.Qty * im.UnitCost)
FROM dbo.InventoryMovement im WHERE im.MovementAt >= @From AND im.MovementAt < @To
workload.plan: Index Seek (range) IX_IM_MovementAt, Hash Match Aggregate in batch mode on rowstore; about 279M rows.

sql: SELECT im.ProductId, im.WarehouseId, SUM(im.Qty), SUM(im.Qty * im.UnitCost) FROM dbo.InventoryMovement im
WHERE im.MovementType = 3 AND im.MovementAt >= @From GROUP BY im.ProductId, im.WarehouseId;
workload.plan: Index Seek (range) IX_IM_MovementAt, Filter (MovementType = 3), Hash Aggregate.

sql: SELECT DATEPART(hour, im.MovementAt), im.MovementType, COUNT(*), SUM(im.Qty) FROM dbo.InventoryMovement im
WHERE im.WarehouseId = @WarehouseId AND im.MovementAt >= @From GROUP BY DATEPART(hour, im.MovementAt), im.MovementType;
SELECT TOP (200) im.MovementAt, im.Qty, im.MovementType, im.ReferenceId FROM dbo.InventoryMovement im
WHERE im.ProductId = @ProductId AND im.WarehouseId = @WarehouseId ORDER BY im.MovementAt DESC;

facts: dbo.InventoryMovement: 1.12B rows, 3.1M rows a day, append-only: no updates and no deletes. Rows arrive in MovementAt order.
The two reporting indexes, IX_IM_MovementAt and IX_IM_WarehouseId_MovementAt, take 85.5 GB together.
Q14 reads about 279M rows per call, 768 times a day, on the primary: there is no readable secondary.
The weekly maintenance job rebuilt both reporting indexes on 2026-09-20; that run generated 131 GB of log and held the log at its cap for almost four hours.

create.why: Three aggregate reports scan hundreds of millions of rows. A columnstore index gives compression, batch mode and row group elimination on MovementAt, which arrives in order.

decisions.why: It serves the stock card: 210,000 ordered seeks a day at 6 reads each. A columnstore index does not replace a seek.

must_not_create.why: About 40 GB more rowstore on a 1.12B-row table for one report that runs 96 times a day.

harmful_removals.why: The stock card would scan a billion-row table 210,000 times a day.
It is the primary key and the clustered index of the table.

key.reference_notes: The two reporting rowstore indexes can go only after the reports are seen to use the columnstore index and a month-end cycle has passed. That later removal is not scored here.
